aid.value: All incoming applicants, including international students, receive automatic merit consideration. Need-based aid requires CSS for international applicants; no universal full-need promise is stated. The separately nominated Hult Scholar Grant aims to cover tuition for up to 10% of entrants, not everyone's living costs. Awards require timely confirmation and full-time good academic/conduct standing for renewal. Boston's published 2027–28 tuition/program charges and living estimates differ from London/Dubai; first-year Boston housing is mandatory. Confirm campus-specific costs and the individual award before committing.

attributes.aidShort: Merit and CSS-based aid; nominated tuition grants, not universal full cost

evidence.quote: Every applicant—whether first-year, transfer, or international—is automatically considered

testing.value: Undergraduate SAT/ACT submissions are optional. Academic records and the required personal assessment interview remain part of review; English proficiency is a separate requirement.

english.value: Non-native speakers must provide English-proficiency evidence. The compulsory online assessment interview can also assess English when needed. The current undergraduate page gives no exam-specific minimums; do not substitute master's or old brochure scores. Ask the enrollment advisor which evidence is accepted for your campus/program.

evidence.quote: Evidence of English proficiency (if not a native speaker)

deadline.value: September 2027 entry: application rounds November 1, 2026, December 15, 2026 and March 1, 2027; late applicants June 1. April 1 is a transfer deadline, not an ordinary first-year round. January 2027 entry: October 1 and November 1, 2026. Complete all required steps, including interview, for review. September offers normally require confirmation May 1, 2027 or within two weeks for decisions afterwards; January offers use two weeks. Follow the individual offer deadline.

aid.value: The current international aid page offers the $6,000/year Lotus award specifically to undergraduate transfers. President's full-tuition and Dean's half-tuition awards are listed for continuing students, not guaranteed incoming first-years. Graduate and monastic IBEF awards have separate program eligibility and must not be presented as general bachelor's aid. Scholarship deadlines are separate from admission. Current undergraduate pages focus on transfers; confirm first-year availability and any award in writing before planning to enroll.

attributes.aidShort: Transfer Lotus award; full-tuition award is for continuing students

english.value: Non-native undergraduate applicants need official TOEFL/IELTS evidence, or may request UWest's remote English Placement Test for $50. Direct entry without EPT: older-scale TOEFL 69+ with reading/listening/speaking 16 and writing 18; IELTS Academic 5.5 with reading/listening 5.0 and speaking/writing 6.0. Conditional entry with EPT lists TOEFL 59–68 or IELTS 5.0 and separate section thresholds. The page has no new 2026 TOEFL scale; ask admissions rather than converting it. Current undergraduate application guidance focuses on transfers, so confirm first-year eligibility.

evidence.quote: Undergraduate Degree Programs, EPT not required 69 & above

fee.value: The international undergraduate checklist requires a non-refundable application fee, but this page does not publish the amount or a waiver. Confirm the charge in the application before payment. The $50 remote English placement test is a separate fee, not the application fee. Current undergraduate pages focus on transfers; confirm whether a first-year application is available.

aid.value: International aid may combine academic scholarships, need-based grants and campus work, without packaged loans. Seven competitive Global Scholarships cover tuition, room, board and university fees for four consecutive years; first-years receive priority. This is not a universal full-cost or full-need promise. Budget about $5,000 first-year indirect costs; travel, insurance, books, visa/SEVIS and possible taxes are outside covered direct costs. Request need-based aid during admission through CSS 1842: no CSS fee waivers or substitute forms. Non-aid applicants use Certificate of Finances. Aid cannot first be requested after admission or in later years; financial documents go through the portal, not email.

attributes.aidShort: Seven competitive direct-cost Global awards; CSS aid; indirect costs excluded

evidence.quote: We do not package international students with loans.

testing.value: International first-year applicants may choose SAT/ACT-optional review in Common App or self-report scores without a reporting fee. English-proficiency evidence and financial documents are separate requirements.

english.value: International applicants and those educated outside the US need an English exam or an approved waiver. Recommended minimums: DET 115+, IELTS 7.0+, older TOEFL 95+; no new-scale TOEFL threshold is published. Scores must be within two years and are not superscored. Applicant self-reports are not accepted; agency delivery or specified school-sent complete reports are required. Request a waiver through the portal after application, using eligible exams or four years of English-medium high school with B+ in all four English-course years. Do not copy the page's anomalous ACT raw-score guidance without confirmation. TOEFL Home Edition is accepted, MyBest/iTP Plus and IELTS Indicator are not.

evidence.quote: We do not provide waivers until the applicant submits the above form.

fee.value: The first-year international checklist explicitly provides a free Common Application. This does not waive CSS Profile, visa, English-testing or document costs; Sewanee separately states it provides no CSS fee waivers.

deadline.value: International first-year applications: ED I November 15, EA December 1, ED II January 15, RD February 1. Supporting documents, including financial documents: November 19, December 6, January 21 and February 8 respectively. ED agreements must accompany the application. International deposit dates in the table are January 15, April 1, March 1 and April 1 respectively; do not assume a domestic May 1 deadline. The table does not label an entry year: confirm the intended cycle and allow document-processing time.

aid.value: The current international aid/checklist pages state assessed need is met through grants, merit and campus work, with need-aware competitive admission; merit ranges $20,000 to full tuition. https://catalog.rhodes.edu/general-information/admission instead says Rhodes strives to meet need and gives a $20,000–$40,000 merit range. Confirm the guarantee and award ceiling before relying on either. Both use the Rhodes financial supplement, not compulsory CSS/FAFSA. The international page requires a supporting bank statement and excludes transport, books, SEVIS, personal expenses and break housing. No full-cost guarantee or zero-family-contribution assumption is approved.

evidence.quote: Our international admission process is need-aware

testing.value: SAT/ACT are optional for ordinary international first-year admission. Applicants without scores may be asked for a virtual interview. The English exam requirement remains separate. The catalog's special Early Admission plan for students enrolling before high-school completion has separate testing requirements; it is not ordinary Early Decision.

english.value: Non-native speakers submit TOEFL, IELTS or DET. Competitive recommendations, not universal cutoffs: new TOEFL 5.0 (95 on pre-January-2026 tests), IELTS 7.0, DET 130. English-medium secondary education can support a waiver; the catalog specifies at least two years as primary instructional language. Confirm waiver eligibility with admissions. Official exam delivery is stated in https://catalog.rhodes.edu/general-information/admission. Outside interviews are recommended but not compulsory and may carry separate costs.

evidence.quote: Applicants most competitive for admission are recommended

fee.value: The current online admissions catalog explicitly says no first-year or transfer application fee is required. This does not waive optional interview services, exam delivery or financial/visa document costs.

evidence.quote: No application fee is required for first-year or transfer students.

deadline.value: Both current admissions pages and https://catalog.rhodes.edu/general-information/admission agree on ED I November 1, EA November 15 and ED II/RD January 15 application dates. But the website requires the ED deposit within two weeks of notification, whereas the catalog gives December 1 and February 15; decision schedules also differ. Confirm the actual offer and financial-document deadlines. International aid uses the Rhodes supplement, not the generic FAFSA instructions; no entry year is labelled in these tables.

evidence.quote: must make a $500 enrollment deposit within two weeks of notification.
